Unproved Stem Cell Clinics Proliferate in the U.S.

I'm surprised to see an influx of these articles talking about the clinics. As someone who interacts with them, I feel like this is being crocked up to expand the power and income of the FDA more than to protect consumers. I believe there are some bad eggs out there overstating their claims, but when it comes down to it we won't know long term effects without using these therapies, and the treatments are highly effective for several conditions when applied and performed properly... which is why they are a pretty big threat to big pharma profits (which basically fund the FDA).

Also, doctors doing autologous treatments without expansion fall under the jurisdiction of state medical boards. It really isn't the FDA's business because autologous treatments for homologous use are not a drug, they are not a biologic, they aren't even a tissue product (though those are used in conjunction sometimes). It is a person's own cells being used in a clinical procedure. Other than the claims made in marketing and on websites, the FDA has no clout if for no other reason, then because there is no interstate trade occurring (because no actual product is being used). I think they are going to get their way, but it is so ridiculous for them to claim jurisdiction.

Also the man who had the growth received cells from Russia. Even if you feel the efficacy of these treatments has not been proven, isn't it better to have some local control over quality? The war on drugs has spread to the war on stem cells. Both are complete bullshit.
